ALG-H4-11.new_tell: Three of the four options (30, 42, 54) form an arithmetic run with common difference 12 and 48 sits off it. That makes 48 the shape-outlier, which points a pattern-guesser AWAY from the key, so it is not exploitable - but it is a regularity that was not there to be created before the repair, and it means the key is now one of three evenly spaced values. Second, minor: the option set spans exactly [30, 60), the whole legal range for 'the larger number', which tells a student the intended reading is that the larger number is what is being reported (i.e. it quietly confirms you have not been asked for 3s). Neither rises to a solve-without-work tell.
ALG-H4-11.note: Constraint 3s >= (60-s)+12 gives s >= 18, so L = 60-s <= 42, attained at s=18 (54 = 42+12). Key confirmed. Unbounded-domain check: the stem never says the numbers are integers, and it does not need to - the maximum sits at the continuous boundary s=18, which is itself integral, so the integer and real readings give the same 42. No second option becomes defensible under either domain. Two-route check on each distractor: 48 requires attaching the 12 to the smaller side (3s+12 >= L), unreachable from any legitimate parse of 'at least 12 more than the larger number'; 54 is 3s at the boundary, not a value of the larger number at all; 30 is the minimum rather than the maximum. None has a second, legitimate route. Magnitude check (the repaired defect): every option lies in [30, 60), the range the sum-60 / larger-of-two condition already fixes, so nothing is eliminable by kind or magnitude without algebra - this looks correctly repaired. One residual softness in 30: if 'the larger number' is read strictly, 30 forces both numbers equal and there is no larger number, so a careful student can retire 30 on structural grounds - but that still takes the sum insight, not zero algebra, so it does not make the set weak. Difficulty: a single translation into one linear inequality, 4s >= 72, then subtract. The only real trap is reporting 3s instead of 60-s. That is standard module-2 fare, not the top of the hard route.

ALG-H4-22.new_tell: The option set is 1, 2, 3, 4 - consecutive integers starting at the stem's own lower bound. That gives away the scale of the answer and converts the item from an inequality into four arithmetic checks: a student who never writes 60+45m > 60m can just tabulate 105/60, 150/120, 195/180, 240/240 and count, because the options guarantee the crossing is at or below m=4. This is the one thing the repair introduced that changes how the item is solved. It does not break exclusivity (the brute-force route lands on 3, and it still requires noticing that m=4 is a tie, which is the actual trap), but it caps the difficulty. If you want this at hard-route difficulty, widen the options so the count is not pre-bounded.
ALG-H4-22.note: 60+45m > 60m reduces to 60 > 15m, m < 4, so m in {1,2,3} and the answer is 3. Key confirmed. Unbounded/unstated-domain check (the repaired defect): the stem now pins both ends - 'whole-number values of m' and 'm is at least 1' - and the inequality supplies the upper bound, so the counted set is finite and unambiguous. This reads as a clean repair of exactly that defect. 4 is defensible ONLY under >=, and the stem says 'greater than', so it is excluded by the stem's own word; at m=4 both clubs cost 240 and neither is greater. 2 requires starting the count at m=2, which the stem forbids with 'm is at least 1'. 1 comes from dividing 60 by 45 rather than by the 15-dollar rate difference. Two-route check: I looked specifically for a second legitimate reading that would land on 2 - the natural candidate is treating the joining month as already paid, cost 60+45(m-1); that gives 15+45m > 60m, m < 1, and counts ZERO values, not 2, so it does not rescue any option. 'One-time joining fee' also blocks that reading outright. Magnitude check: all four options are legal counts of a subset of {1,2,3,...}, none is the wrong kind of quantity or outside a stated total. Difficulty: two linear models, one strict inequality, one boundary subtlety at the tie. The tie is the only thing separating it from routine, and the narrow option set lets a student sidestep the algebra entirely - medium.
